channel.title: Global Arbitration Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Arbitration Review (globalarbitrationreview.com)

item.title: K&L Gates adds partner in Sydney
item.description: Energy disputes and investigations lawyer Peter Brabant has left Charles Russell Speechlys to join the partnership at K&L Gates in Sydney.

item.title: Squire Patton Boggs partner shifts to Singapore to lead Asia energy practice
item.description: Squire Patton Boggs partner Max Rockall has relocated from London to Singapore to lead the firm’s Asia-Pacific energy disputes and LNG practice.

item.title: More e-commerce investors pursue Korea
item.description: More US investment management firms have joined a group of e-commerce investors threatening to file an investment treaty claim against South Korea over its response to a customer data leak from the country’s largest online retailer.

item.title: Keystone hires two more from Clyde & Co
item.description: Milena Szuniewicz-Wenzel and Ian Hopkinson have left Clyde & Co to join the partnership at Keystone Law in London, after Ben Knowles made the same move last week.

item.title: US appeal court rejects Russia’s immunity defence to Crimea awards
item.description: A US appeal court has rejected Russia’s attempt to use sovereign immunity to halt enforcement of two investment treaty awards concerning the seizure of assets in Crimea.

item.title: Who is sitting at ICSID?
item.description: Fourteen panels have formed at ICSID in recent weeks, including first-time appointments for Senegalese academic Makane Moïse Mbengue and Stuart Isaacs KC of Wilberforce Chambers.

item.title: ICC registered nearly 900 new cases in 2025
item.description: The ICC International Court of Arbitration's latest case figures reveal that 894 new cases were registered with the institution in 2025, making the year among its top three in terms of case volume, while it also issued it second highest annual total of approved awards - 607 over the year.

item.title: French supreme court shields Libyan assets frozen by sanctions
item.description: France’s Court of Cassation has affirmed that those seeking to attach sovereign assets frozen by EU sanctions must first obtain approval from the French Treasury – rejecting an appeal by a Kuwaiti construction company trying to enforce a billion-dollar award against Libya.

item.title: Pinsent Masons hires from WilmerHale in London
item.description: Cem Kalelioğlu, who helped obtain the first known investment treaty award against China, has left WilmerHale to join the partnership at Pinsent Masons in London.

item.title: Arms dealer fails to halt LCIA cases over Ukraine contracts
item.description: A UK court has declined to stay two LCIA arbitrations relating to high-value contracts for the supply of artillery rounds and rockets to Ukraine while the sole arbitrator is challenged over his refusal to hold an evidentiary hearing.
